clue.text: Merseyside singer, fellow associated with Parisian group, getting a fiddle

parts.note: Gerry Marsden, frontman of Gerry and the Pacemakers from Liverpool
a fellow is a man
a Parisian word is French, and de is the French for of
a ring is a group or gang

explanation.surface: A Liverpool pop star and his French connection end up in some kind of swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: GERRY Marsden led Gerry and the Pacemakers, a 1960s Liverpool band. 'Parisian' gives a French word, DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Redrawing electoral boundaries for party advantage is a political swindle, a fiddle in British slang.

clue.text: Our backers who watch over us to keep us safe?

definitions.text: who watch over us to keep us safe?

parts.note: the puzzle appears in the Guardian newspaper, so 'our' is that paper
angels are financial backers, especially of theatre shows

explanation.surface: Those supporting us also look after our safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' is the setter speaking as the Guardian; theatrical investors are called angels.
explanation.definitionFit: Protective spirits believed to watch over each person are known by this phrase.

clue.text: Hold back material about German police force

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
re means about or concerning
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary police force

explanation.surface: Fabric concerning the Nazi police is being withheld.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain or suppress something is a synonym of holding it back.

clue.text: Who is upset, first to cry, a bit cowardly?

indicators.note: says the word for cry is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: to yell is to cry out

indicators.note: upset means knocked out of order, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about someone who, distressed, is the first to weep and so seems somewhat timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to' looks like a selection of C from 'cry', but it places the whole synonym of cry at the front; 'upset' rearranges WHO IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and the -ish suffix softens it to somewhat.

clue.text: State of a girl half-cut, having obtained two degrees

indicators.note: cutting half means losing the second half of the word for girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
BA and MA are Bachelor and Master of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: A tipsy young woman with two university qualifications is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' (British for drunk) here cuts LASS in half to LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the southern states of the USA.

clue.text: Learner-driver and vehicle flipping over in river — disaster!

indicators.note: in places the flipped letters inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: flipping over turns the learner and the vehicle backwards

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a learner driver's car
a cab is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A learner's car overturns into a river: a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping over' turns L+CAB into BACL, which goes 'in' DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating collapse or fiasco.

clue.text: Republicans want it done away with — an audible torrent?

definitions.text: Republicans want it done away with

indicators.note: an audible one is the word spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a torrent of water from the sky is heavy rain

explanation.surface: Anti-monarchists want something abolished; is it a downpour you can hear?
explanation.definitionFit: Republicans oppose monarchy, so they want a sovereign's rule abolished.

clue.text: Dance follows final game

indicators.note: follows puts the word for dance after the word for final

parts.note: net is the final amount after deductions
a ball is a dance

explanation.surface: A dance takes place after the championship final.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport played with a ball and raised hoops.

clue.text: Theresa is repeating bid to sort out national problem

indicators.note: sorting out the letters means rearranging them
repeating means the little word is used twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Theresa May keeps making attempts to fix the country's trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeating' doubles IS before 'to sort out' shuffles all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase was once used for Britain's supposed chronic ailment of industrial strikes.

clue.text: Everyone out of bed, mum brought round flask

indicators.note: bringing round turns the words backwards

parts.note: all up means everyone has risen
ma is mum

explanation.surface: With everyone up, Mum fetches a flask.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampulla is a small round two-handled flask of ancient times.

clue.text: Skin problem requiring British surgeon

parts.note: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A dermatological issue needing a British doctor's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised bubble of fluid under the skin is a common minor ailment.

clue.text: What's thrown game — his handling of the ball?

parts.note: a die is thrown in board games
Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A question about a footballer handling the ball after something is thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: Diego Maradona scored with his hand in the 1986 World Cup, the 'Hand of God' goal; the definition is a riddling description of him.
explanation.definitionFit: The handball goal by Maradona is the most famous instance of a footballer illegally using a hand.

clue.text: Like jargon about final aim that's gaining influence

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: about means the jargon word goes around the aim

parts.note: cant is specialist jargon
an end is a final aim or goal

explanation.surface: Specialist language about one's goal seems to be gaining ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the rise in power or dominance is the adjectival sense here.

clue.text: Four in a car sleep when it's warm

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the car

parts.note: an estate is an estate car, a station wagon
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people dozing in a car on a hot day.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is British for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that go dormant through summer heat are said to do this, the opposite of hibernating.

clue.text: Son in Brittany collects English records

indicators.note: collects means the son word takes in the English letter

parts.note: fils is French for son, and Brittany is in France

explanation.surface: A Breton son gathers English documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Files are stored documents or records.

clue.text: Cheerful end to negotiation after manoeuvring — an impossible treat?

indicators.note: manoeuvring means the letters are moved about into a new order
the end to a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Happy that talks have concluded with some smart moves, someone gets a treat that cannot exist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end to' takes N, the last of 'negotiation', for 'after manoeuvring' to shuffle with CHEERFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'there's no such thing as a free lunch' means nothing truly comes without cost.

clue.text: A desire that a cockney may initially lack?

definitions.text: that a cockney may initially lack?

parts.note: an itch is a craving or desire

explanation.surface: A longing that a Londoner might be missing at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop the H sound at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H is spelt out as this word, and is what gets dropped at the start of cockney words.

clue.text: Dig in Derby maybe, having turned up in a shawl

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, backwards
in places the digging word inside the hat

parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat
to till is to dig the soil

explanation.surface: Someone digs in Derby and turns up wearing a shawl.
explanation.walkthrough: TILL goes 'in' HAT to give HTILLAT, which 'having turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallith is the fringed prayer shawl worn by Jewish men.

clue.text: Thus the dinner was complete, as forecast?

definitions.meaning: the after-dinner port marked the meal's close

explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to foreshadow, so the past tense means foretold.

clue.text: Muscular problem the old man has to fight against endlessly

parts.note: pa is dad, one's old man

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to resist is to fight against

explanation.surface: Father has a muscle complaint he keeps battling.
explanation.definitionFit: Paresis is partial paralysis or weakness of muscles.

clue.text: Thief who can be heard going through papers

definitions.text: who can be heard going through papers
definitions.meaning: someone making a crackling noise while leafing through papers

explanation.definitionFit: A livestock thief has this name, and anyone making a crackling paper noise does too.

clue.text: Some from Provence with piano tune conveying gloom

parts.note: des is French for some, and Provence is in France
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A melancholy Provençal tune played on the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopelessness and deep gloom are close synonyms.

clue.text: Awfully large lad is losing energy in dances

indicators.note: awfully suggests a mess, so the letters are rearranged
losing means a letter is dropped from the word large

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy big boy runs out of steam at the dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops E from LARGE; 'Awfully' then shuffles LARG, LAD and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Galliards are lively sixteenth-century court dances.

clue.text: Be enthralled by this person's contribution to framework

indicators.note: enthralled by means held within the other piece

parts.note: this person is the setter, I, and the 's is am, so I am

explanation.surface: Be captivated by what this person contributes to a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person's' is read as I'm, I AM, which holds BE.
explanation.definitionFit: An I-shaped steel girder is a standard part of building frameworks.

clue.text: Combat zone held by royalist supporters

indicators.note: held by means the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A battlefield occupied by backers of the king.
explanation.definitionFit: The lists were the enclosed ground for medieval jousting tournaments.

clue.text: See one taking rest — unfortunately doesn't get on with it

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Look at someone taking a break; sadly, they are not getting on with the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dawdling or hanging about idly is not getting on with the task.

clue.text: Insect in road nibbling end off a plant

indicators.note: in places the insect inside the shortened road
nibbling the end off removes the last letter of the road word

parts.note: a lane is a road
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect on a road chews the tip off a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nibbling end off' removes the road's final E before 'in' places the insect just after its first letter; the closing 'a' is added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Lantana is a flowering tropical shrub of the verbena family.

clue.text: The anthem's roar disturbed this writer with centuries of meditations

definitions.text: this writer with centuries of meditations

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loud anthem upsets a contemplative writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centuries of Meditations' is the actual title of his best-known prose work.
explanation.definitionFit: Traherne was a seventeenth-century English poet and cleric known for his work called Centuries of Meditations.
